quest.title: After the Peace
quest.description: Tonight, you hear a familiar voice in your dreams...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Return to your accommodation and rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lately we've been sleeping well, and eating even better... now this is the life!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About time we got to live like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Heehee, look, Paimon's tummy is so stuffed, it's all round and plump now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* —And now it's time for some rest! Mmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What a peaceful feeling... We're normally so busy, it's nice to have some downtime like this every once in a while between adventures.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We've got trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That voice... is that Citlali?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To hear your voice at a time like this is truly an honor, Granny Itztli...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Cut that out, it's serious! And what are you doing sleeping this late? Who are you, me?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Come see us in the Speaker's Chamber once you've cleaned yourselves up. We're waiting for you here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So much for sleeping in... Guess we'll have to head over there.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wake up, Paimon, we've gotta go find Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nooo, Paimon's not done eating yet... Huh? Oh... Good morning...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After explaining the situation to Paimon, you quickly wash up and head to the Speaker's Chamber...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I wonder if they've eaten... Or if they've even gotten up... Hmm, maybe I should buy some snacks?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, don't tell me something came up on their way here...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Relax. I'm sure they're fine.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, there they are!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: See, just like I said.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mavuika, Citlali! We came running as soon as we got your message!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you for coming all this way. Here, have some water and catch your breath first.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like something major happened.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, you could certainly say that... I'll let Citlali explain.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem... Strictly speaking, I'm just passing on something I heard as well. Basically, the Wayob passed a truly shocking piece of news to me through the smoke last night.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're aware that Mavuika's not the first Pyro Archon, yes? On occasion, there were those who lived longer than an ordinary human, not unlike my situation. But, all in all, the title has changed hands many times.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And now, the Wayob have sensed a special surge within the Ley Lines. A truly ancient soul is about to return to the mortal realm.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: His name... is Xbalanque.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xbalanque!? But isn't he... Isn't he the very very first...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, that's him. The first Pyro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: According to legend, he was the greatest of heroes and leaders, and the one who made a deal with the Ruler of Death, thereby creating the rules that saved Natlan's Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hasn't he been dead like, a really long time? How can he be resurrected?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even in Natlan, it's impossible for someone as ancient as him to ever return... Still, nothing's off the table when Xbalanque's concerned.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hence, why this really is "something major."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let me be clear about this: I did not mishear, nor is the Wayob mistaken! We would never jest about something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, both {NICKNAME} and I have complete faith in your abilities. Whose interpretation of the Wayob's will could we trust, if not yours?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the one thing I'll never be modest about. But the fact I'm not wrong about this only further begs the question — just why is Lord Xbalanque suddenly about to be resurrected now?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As you can see, Citlali's even more concerned about this than I am.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Still, it's understandable. Waiting to find out the whole truth must be torture for a great shaman who can only peep at the outcomes without knowing the causes.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Mavuika, I hope you'll approach this with a measure of caution. Depending on how things go, everything could change, or nothing at all... I think you know what I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I do. Xbalanque's arrival will shake our nation. After all, we still don't know if he's satisfied with the outcome of this war.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, do you think he'll come and find you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah! You can't just up and say things like that, you scared me half to death!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's actually pretty likely. Think about it, people in the same line of work tend to have some similarities, right? Maybe all Pyro Archons share my disposition.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I don't want to meet him! I—I haven't really mentally prepared myself yet for such a... grand occasion!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Anyway, my job was just to pass on the message and bring {NICKNAME} over. Now that that's dealt with, you can discuss the Pilgrimage. I'm done here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! Where are you going, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Back to bed! You have no idea how much that scared me — I was up all night... Ugh, I can barely keep my eyes open... Nighty night.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright then, what's this about the Pilgrimage?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's like I said before. Our cultural legacy shouldn't end with our triumph over our suffering. Instead, it will burn brighter than ever.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame has been given new meaning. We have chosen to turn it into a pure athletic competition, promoting fair play and encouraging the personal growth of contestants.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And... this grand tournament will begin soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woo! That sounds awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm itching to sign up!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Heroes are drawn to tournaments like this, and naturally, you're no exception.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The news of Lord Xbalanque's impending resurrection may be a bombshell, but I believe that we should keep our focus on the Pilgrimage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, okay... So, not in a hurry to find him, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. I have already informed the tribes that we'll be hosting the next tournament right away. It'll help sweep away the shadows cast by the war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Preparing supplies, cleaning up and remodeling the competition venues, recruiting staff for logistics, moral support, and pre-tournament weather forecasting... All of that's been assigned. We need to make sure everything is completed well and on schedule first.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. You are our cherished friends, and a part of our nation, and I would like to invite you to serve as special supervisors for this event.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon can do it, too?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Of course. On that note, my two new supervisors, would you come with me to check on the progress of each of the tribes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure!

talks.objective: Go to the People of the Springs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! This is our first stop.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, looks like someone's in a good mood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Paimon's here as a special supervisor this time! Hehe, it's only been a few days, but Paimon's back and cooler than ever!

choices.text: I'm sorry, Paimon can be a lot...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ah, it's nothing. We've got a long road ahead, so it's good that she's so motivated.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Pretty much all we need to do is talk to everyone and confirm how the preparations for the Pilgrimage are going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold a sec, take a look over there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See that? Someone's fishing... Ah, it's them!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ah, our iconic trio.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: It's a quartet, you insolent ignoramuses, a quartet! How dare you treat the Almighty Dragonlord like a subhuman? If anything, I'm superhuman! ...Wait, no, draconian!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Why, hello there, Ajaw, and you three. What are you up to?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: We're fishing, Archon! Mualani says if we're lucky, we might catch someone really special!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Yeah, like that punk, Xbalanque. Pah! He's such a pathetic little— Gwargh!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: My apologies. Ajaw clearly hasn't earned his ticket to see the sun today. We didn't mean any offense — when Kachina and Mualani were talking about "fishing," they meant it literally, with hook and bait.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Lowly servant! How dare you beat up the Almighty Dragonlord for some ancient fogey that you only know by name! You'll pay for this... I'll start with some chili in your water skin...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ah, so you've heard about his impending return. Did Citlali mention that to you?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Mhm, we ran into her on the road not too long ago. She seemed to be falling asleep standing up, and kept mumbling about something...

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: "Oh no, oh no, why is Xbalanque coming back now? Did we screw something up? We couldn't have, right? But what else could have alarmed him so much..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that sounds just like her...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: And now that you're done, scram.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Wah!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: To be honest, it's been bothering me quite a lot... Under normal circumstances, it shouldn't be possible for us to meet Lord Xbalanque, right? So... does this mean something's wrong?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: As you can see, there are many people that are thinking along those same lines. I believe that...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hey! We've got a bite!

response.speaker: Drowning Man
response.text: Help! Help! Something's pulling on me!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's what's going to save your life! Are you having leg cramps?

response.speaker: Drowning Woman
response.text: I... *gurgle* *gurgle*...! Help... *gurgle*

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hold your breath for now! We'll get you out right away!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: With everyone's help, you manage to rescue the drowning people...

response.speaker: Drowning Man
response.text: Ugh... *coughing*

response.speaker: Drowning Woman
response.text: *cough* Thank you... so much, everyone... Wait, why is our Archon here... too... *cough*

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well, would you look at that... You actually caught some people after all.

response.speaker: Drowning Woman
response.text: Thanks for your help... Otherwise, that sudden bout of leg cramps might have ended our entire surfing squad.

response.speaker: Drowning Woman
response.text: The two of us are in charge of transporting supplies. After safely delivering some of the equipment, medicine, and a few other things for the tournament, we had some time to spare, so...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Didn't warm up before going into the water, did ya?

response.speaker: Drowning Man
response.text: Thank you, thank you so much... We'll, um, leave you to it, then.

response.speaker: Drowning Woman
response.text: We'll never forget how you saved us! We know you're busy, though, so no need to worry about us — we'll see you around!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you gotta give it to Mualani, when she wants something to happen, then it just happens...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Then it won't be long before she reels in Xbalanque himself. Now that'll be a wonder of wonders...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehehe, I was just thinking, what if he enjoyed swimming like the rest of us? It's easy enough for anyone who loves the water to end up here, so might as well give it a try. It'd be a great chance to say hi to him!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I used some commemorative badges for the Stadium as a special bait. He's never been to present-day Natlan, so it'll all be new to him! I'm sure he'll be thrilled.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And before you say anything — anything's possible! On the off chance this'll work, it's worth a try no matter how unlikely it is! Just like playing the lottery.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: As you can see, the power of friendship sustains their faith in the theory.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well, what about you, then? Given your personality, isn't your continued presence a testament to the power of friendship, too?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Haha, she saw right through you, my foolish lackey! Silly, naive child... Now, witness the scorn of K'uhul Aja—owww!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Picking up where we left off before... Citlali never makes mistakes with her messages, so I believe... that it would be best for you to meet with Lord Xbalanque. That should quell any unnecessary speculation.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Thanks. I'll keep that in mind.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But for now, what I need to do is check on the status of the preparations for the upcoming Pilgrimage.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: ...Hmm, seems like the People of the Springs have done a great job.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yup, don't worry! We only came here to fish after finishing all of our work. We're all done, all three of us!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Mhm! Everyone at the Children of Echoes has been hard at work too. I only came here after finishing my tasks for today. It looked like everyone else was about finished too.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Same for the Scions of the Canopy. We're all wrapped up.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now that's efficiency. I trust you. Well, looks like we won't have to make the trip to your tribes then.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Everyone, this iteration of the Pilgrimage holds great importance to Natlan as it is now. We must pull together and work as one, creating the best atmosphere possible for all our participants.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Uh-huh, suuure. Dunno why you'd worry about this stuff. You're always so ready to pounce on and fight just about anything — why, you even dare to disrespect the almighty Dragonlord!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Remind me again, has Ajaw done anything besides talk?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I'll send the dirtiest jobs his way right this instant.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: What are you doing to me, you son of a—!? Hey! Let me go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's always a party with those three! Seems like we can check off the People of the Springs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, four. Sorry, those four.

choices.text: I'm sorry, Paimon's letting this get to her head again...

talks.objective: Go to the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! There she is! Right over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali! Didn't you say you were going to get some more sleep? Why are you still here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* The Chief came to me for help just now. Not like I can just ignore someone in need and go back to bed, now can I?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You didn't tell him that you stayed up all night?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I just told him about Xbalanque's imminent return, and told him to be prepared. There was no need to mention anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, you've still got a reputation to maintain, huh? Can't have people thinking Granny Itztli would lose sleep over something like this!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh, now you're making fun of me too, huh? Hmph, so even children are ridiculing me now. This cannot stand...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And you! Do you also think I'm just trying to keep up appearances?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nope, not me, would never think that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And you too! What about you, Mavuika?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No, no, of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Relax, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Xbalanque was no ordinary person. He loved this land as much as we do, and managed to forge a miracle through the Ruler of Death. I don't think he'll give us too hard a time.

choices.text: Even though I've never known him...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: *sigh* If that's what even the two of you think, then my worrying seems even more unnecessary. Alright, alright, I get it. That's just the kind of paranoid old hag I am.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That means I can go get some shut-eye, then? You can take a look around yourselves. And if you need any help, feel free to go find the Chief, or Ororon.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The Chief should be overseeing the preparation of the woven scrolls required for the tournament right about now, and as for Ororon... I believe he said he was going to do some handicrafts at the valley entrance.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, come on, you're making it sound like it's my first time here. Rest well, and stop worrying so much. We'll discuss the tournament with Ororon.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Alright, then. Good night, everyone. And don't go thinking that Granny Itztli doesn't like hanging out with you just because she's not around all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Huh? Mavuika? Oh, shoot. What are you doing here...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Xilonen? What a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey there, Xilonen! Did you come here for work?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ororon... Did he sell me out? I thought I asked him to not tell anyone that I was here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, he didn't mention you at all!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Tch... That so.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: *sigh* She's avoiding me. There are a few big pieces of equipment we need for the tournament, and I've been wanting to ask her to make them.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I went straight to her place because I was worried she might refuse, but each time, there was nobody home, and the neighbors said that she was busy... turns out she was here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Xilonen's tent is nearby too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, she literally ran away from home just to avoid taking work from you!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hrmm...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Okay, that's enough about me... What are you here for? Checking on Pilgrimage prep progress?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes, and to see how everyone's doing while we're at it. Still, most everyone we've talked to so far has been pretty interested in Xbalanque.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Xbalanque? Did you just say Xbalanque?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, have you been so busy running away that you missed the whole memo about him?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain Xbalanque's imminent resurrection to Xilonen...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm still trying to wrap my head around it... But if that's what Citlali said, then it has to be true.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Everyone's reactions make sense, too. Who wouldn't want to see the first Archon?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: This isn't a bad time for it to happen, either. The war has only just ended, and with their long-standing goal suddenly gone, people are feeling a little lost.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I met a warrior from the People of the Springs near the Speaker's Chamber a few days ago. He spent the entire afternoon pacing around the area.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I asked him if anything was bothering him, and he said that he used to train for battle every afternoon. But now that the crisis is resolved, he doesn't know what to do with himself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon can definitely see that... It's tough when what you've been doing all along suddenly stops being necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why you want to hold the Pilgrimage again, right? To help everyone find a new goal.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's right. We will have competition take the place of ceaseless battle. It will give us an outlet for our pent-up energy, and offer a reward for the blood and sweat we've put into improving and growing.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's the meaning of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame today and in the future.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sounds pretty good to me. I am starting to like this new Pilgrimage already.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But how do you feel, Mavuika?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: About Xbalanque, you mean? Meh, it's okay, I guess.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Shouldn't you be, you know, a little more nervous? He's our nation's progenitor. You sure he's not coming just to supervise your work?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ah, you sound like someone who's finally gotten the chance to strike back after years of oppression.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hey, don't put it like that... Alright, maybe a little. It's not every day that someone who could bring you down a notch shows up.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hahaha, I knew that's what you'd think. Don't worry. If the real Xbalanque does make an appearance, then naturally, I have my ways to meet him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? How?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: No spoilers just yet. Take a guess.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you have a playful side, too?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Of course she does. This whole "glorious, righteous leader" thing is just one facet of her, and it's the side of her you've seen the most so far. But...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Tragically, this is how my long-time companions think of me. Xilonen's always saying how awful I am.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hey, hey! Don't just put words into my mouth like that. I've only ever said that you can be quite terrible "sometimes."

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #Sure, sure, whatever you say. Come on, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's head to our next stop.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Oh, and Xilonen, now that you've been busted, be sure to stop by my office and pick up the documents I left for you. I wrote down everything you need to do for the tournament.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Good night! *snores*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaaaaand she's "fallen asleep," just like that...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well, she's got to wake up eventually. Let's go. Good night, Xilonen, and sleep well.

choices.text: Other than Ororon and his trap, I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Doesn't seem like there's anyone around... They're probably all out and about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean the preparations are going smoothly?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Of course, without a doubt. I'll be honest, I'm more concerned about how everyone's doing than how the preparations are coming along.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The amount of rest they get will directly impact their tournament performance. It's my hope that everyone is eating and sleeping well, so they can enter the Stadium full of anticipation.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm. What are you guys doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Chasca!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's been a while. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Things have been good on my end, too. How about you?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Same old, same old. Back to the grind.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Flying around to break up fights when they break out, taking walks with my family when I'm free... You know, the usual. That said, I haven't had much work to do lately.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I take it that means there haven't been many fights?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah, the war has just ended, and the bonds between people have grown a lot stronger in the process... Hard to start fights like that.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I don't mind, though. More time for me to zone out. I just sit at a lookout point and tend to my weapons... The fresh air is also great for my mood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you've been doing well, then!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Glad to hear that.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Haha, what are you talking about? You should know the ups and downs I've been through better than anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, how have preparations been going here at the Flower-Feather Clan?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's why you're here. In that case, I'll take you someplace where you can see the situation clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Follow me.

talks.objective: Go to the place up high

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hah. So this is the place you had in mind. Quite the view.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You can see our whole camp from up here. We trained like this back when we were fighting against the Abyss, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can see people talking and laughing, some holding boxes, others pushing carts... Even some who're using some kinda special equipment to scan the skies!

dialogues.speaker: Flower-Feather Clan Tribesperson
dialogues.text: Ah! It's you, Pyro Archon — and the heroes of Natlan, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, shucks. "Heroes of Natlan"? Paimon's feeling kinda shy now...

dialogues.speaker: Flower-Feather Clan Tribesperson
dialogues.text: What brings you to the Flower-Feather Clan? Are you here to check on our work for the Pilgrimage?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. Everything going well?

dialogues.speaker: Flower-Feather Clan Tribesperson
dialogues.text: Please rest assured, everything's going off without a hitch. Everyone is in good spirits as well. Coach and her students are also here, so they've been helping out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Coach? Oh, is Iansan here too?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Oho, here to inspect our handiwork, then?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Lots of folks from the Flower-Feather Clan have gone to train for the tournament, and my students just so happened to want to get some exercise, so I brought them along to help.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The rules of this tournament are different from before — we're here to compete, not to select the strongest warriors. Everyone finds that quite novel, and is taking it very seriously, treating it like a completely new type of challenge.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Look, they're all over there.

dialogues.speaker: Flower-Feather Clan Tribespeople
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Yopia
dialogues.text: Please rest completely and totally assured that with us here, we'll get all the tasks done on time, no problem and no questions asked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, they're all so reliable! Like Coach, like student, huh, Iansan?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Haha, you flatter me. We're just here to help.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: These exercises are high-frequency but low-intensity, which is perfect for our training. I helped Ifa bring a whole stack of medical supplies from his clinic to the Stadium yesterday. Didn't even break a sweat, easy-peasy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't even break a sweat, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yeah. Ifa was sure sweating a lot, though. Not that I blame him — doctors don't need to be that physically strong, not even vets.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Especially not compared to the toughest coach in all Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Tough, they say? Stuff like this isn't even intermediate level...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And that's why they call you tough. I respect it, though. I doubt I can think of anything that you can't do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon agrees! In fact, after staying in Natlan for so long, even we've begun to feel like there's nothing we can't do...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So, you think it's something about this place?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, exactly! Now, Paimon often finds herself thinking, "Eh, compared to those super tough battles we fought and won, this is nothing at all!"

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm glad you feel that way. It's not often that people can focus on the silver lining after everything that's happened.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Being optimistic also tends to make people grow happier the longer they live. Keep up that attitude, and you'll go from strength to strength.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm... The wind is rising. I think I hear something on the air.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'll head out on a patrol. Have a nice chat, and just let me know if you need anything.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Sounds good. See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: And she's off... She really comes and goes like the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'd say that it's effortlessly cool moments like this that make her so endearing.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Well, what's next for you? You three look relaxed, so I assume you're pretty much done with all the important stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We've already checked up on each of the tribes' progress. Everything is going smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We didn't quite get around to the Children of Echoes, but from what Kachina says, and seeing how Xilonen's doing, it seems they're fine. No need to check up on them.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, um... that's it for the day. The only thing left to do for the next couple of days is... persuade Xilonen to finish her part of the work.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Haha, oh, I'd love to see the face she'd make if she heard you say that.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Since you have time, why don't you give me a hand? As you already know, Mavuika, I'm responsible for designing the tournament course.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Well, it's almost complete, and I've built a mock course. Want to do a trial run?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you mean... we can get a sneak peek at what the competition will be like!?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Indeed. You know that Mavuika can't personally participate in the tournament, right? As the Archon, she must serve as both host and judge.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: And as special supervisors, you can't sign up, either. So, this is your best chance to experience the course!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Say no more, or my hair might spontaneously combust... Come on, just show us the course already.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Alright, follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hmm, what if I put this piece of rope... here? Oh, and this wooden dummy...
Nuh-uh!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No? Then what about this...
No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice... Sounds like Ororon's talking to someone. Let's go see what he's up to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha up to, Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Oh, hello.
Oh dear! Oh dear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...A bird?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No, a juvenile Qucusaurus. This one looks a little different from the others, though... Yeah, a very special look indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is he your pet, Ororon?
The heck are you on about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, he's quick on his feet. That retort was instant...
For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Huh? Did Paimon just say something wrong?
Oh wow... No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What the heck!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about him. He's just... Erm... How should I describe him...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't tell me he's also some kind of elder...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He definitely seems pretty important...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, he's an assistant at Ifa's clinic, and one of my friends. His name is Cacucu.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: The heck are you on about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that not his name?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh wow... No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like he's just repeating a few sentences over and over...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's what he does. Those are all Ifa's catchphrases, so Cacucu picked them up after hearing them day after day.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The last time I delivered some vegetables to the People of the Springs, I ran into Ajaw, who was there for a soak in the hot springs. Ajaw and Cacucu were stuck in an endless back-and-forth argument.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like a schoolyard squabble...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Eventually, Ajaw got really agitated, and just started immediately shouting "No, YOU!" no matter what Cacucu said!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: How unbelievably childish... No less than I'd expect of Ajaw. Even I have rarely witnessed things like that.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: They went on like that for an entire afternoon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, how do you know that? Did you stay and listen to them the whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yeah, I did. It was so dumb, I couldn't look away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're a more patient man than most...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Anyway... I'm here because I'm trying to capture Xbalanque.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Capture," huh? A... wild choice of words.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hmm... then how about, "hunting for Xbalanque"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, you're trying to do WHAT, now?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: We've never seen someone so ancient come back to life before, right? So I wanted to see if I could intercept him. See? This is the trap that I made.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I've used it before. It's quite good at catching wild animals. Don't worry, though — I've already told everyone that there's a trap here, so they won't get too close.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: See? I even made a notice board.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pff, good luck catching anyone with this... And what are you planning on doing with the poor guy when you catch him, anyway? Stick him in a stew?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, no, I just want to see what he looks like. And then... I'll probably invite him to our tribe as a guest.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll admit, I didn't take you for the actively hospitable sort.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well, a chance like this doesn't come every day. I wanted to give it a try, so I also made these little handicrafts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uhh... He says that, yet all of these look like a hunter's lethal handiwork...)

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I see. In that case, I wish you success. If you do manage to catch a wild Xbalanque, please let me know. I'd love to come and watch the fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, not you too!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If the real Xbalanque does show up, a trap like that won't hurt him. We all have faith in him. After all, he was the first Archon of this land.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's right. That's also why I stuffed several layers of cushions and hay in there. If he really triggers the trap, he can just sprawl out and take a nap.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bro, stop. You're driving Paimon insane over here...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh wow... No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if you've got time for this, then you've finished prepping for the tournament, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You took the words right out of my mouth, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's it. Sorry, I didn't know that's what you wanted to ask about.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: We Masters of the Night-Wind are broadly responsible for the woven scrolls and mental support. I have expertise in exactly neither of those, so... I joined the logistics team.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I provided some amazing supplies. The others even praised me for the quality of my produce, and even asked me about how to grow such great fruits and vegetables. I was very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You've gotten quite good at dealing with people.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yes. I think I've rediscovered a bit of that feeling I had in my childhood.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Seems like things here are going smoothly. In that case, we'll check on how things are going elsewhere. See you later, Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bye, Ororon! Good luck with, uh... capturing Xbalanque...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, so he also knows how to say goodbye... See you later then, bros.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hmm... Alright. See you later, my bros.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Stop looking, I'm genuinely asleep now...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Everyone's been very efficient these past few days. Seems like lots of people are looking forward to participating in the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hah! Why don't you sign up, then? Maybe someone'll manage to knock some sense through your thick skull!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Why don't we all join? It'd be a great chance to kick back and relax!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Relax? You find the idea of a tournament relaxing!? This girl is crazy... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mualani's right. Let's all sign up together!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Huh? Even you? Pah, children. Think you're all grown-up, don't you? In the eyes of the great K'uhul Ajaw, you're still...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Nobody asked. We'll go, you stay.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What!? You little—!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Hey hey, hello there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello. You're Cacucu, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh! So you already know my name. That guy told you, didn't he? Ororon, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Hahaha, he spoke the truth. My name is indeed Cacucu, and I did pick those words up from hearing Ifa repeat them.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: And have you met Ifa before?

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: What, even with all his running around and being everywhere all at once all the time, you've never met him? Guess you must be in tip-top shape, so you've just never needed his services.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: He's out to see some patients, and I had nothing to do, so I came to hang out with Ororon and watch him make his Xbalanque-trap. Absurd, right? He's so crazy, I love him.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Ifa. Ah, right, speaking of Ifa, I need to correct you on one thing.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Judging from how you reacted before... Did you think I couldn't really understand the human language?

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: C'mon, bro, of course that's not true! Hehe! As Saurians go, I already understand more than enough! And not just their words, no, but their body language, too.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: There's a limit to how much I can mimic with my vocal cords — mighty shame, that — but I feel like my cadence should convey my meaning well enough.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: So of course I understand what "No way, bro! Do you even hear yourself?" means — and all the rest of it too. I meant those words from the bottom of my heart.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Also, I'm no pet, I'm Ifa's colleague! Be a good bro, and call me Dr. Cacucu.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You got it, Brocucu.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Hehehe, I like you! Chose the "bro" part over the "doc" part, eh? Well, if you'll be my bro, I'll gladly be yours too.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Ifa and Ororon are both my bros, and now, I've found a third bro. You look like a real fighter, too. Just what the doctor ordered.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Oh, and I guess Ajaw counts for like, half a bro. You know, that useless guy who works for Kinich from the Scions of the Canopy. Ahahaha, he's a funny one. Often chokes half to death on his anger after just a few words.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He often calls himself the "Almighty Dragonlord"...

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Hah! Sorry, what? "Almighty Dragonlord"? Bwahahahahahaha!

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Bro, don't believe a single word he says. He's just an idiot. He'd have gotten himself killed long ago if Kinich wasn't looking out for him!

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Still, don't you think that's what gives life its spice? No matter how much Ajaw whines, he can't leave Kinich. And Ifa can complain all he wants, but Ororon's still his friend.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Oh, and me, too. Ifa often says I'm too familiar with everyone — that I instantly fly off and tell all of my Saurian friends whenever he does something dumb. But that's just how we live, man. We torment and depend on each other in turns.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Once we Saurians know, the humans will know, too. And whatever humans know, the humans from further away will know real soon.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Still, I know you'll love Ifa, bro. He's a good guy, after all. Have you ever met a bad guy who's like, resigned all the time?

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Anyway, if you ever need a doc, or just someone to help you translate our tongue, come find me anytime. I'll send my boy Ifa to go help right away.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Oh oops, I meant "my bro Ifa." Of course I'd slip up. He's not a boy, you hear? He's my bro.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What is it? Do you want to talk about something else?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hmm, you've got to find someone who understands Saurian-tongue to translate for you, then.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Or... transform into a Saurian so they can talk to you. On that note, I'd love to try that one day, bro.
